default.reason: ops-desk: fak Ops worker desk - several workers name GLM 5.3 Flash; the desk routes the middle-ground tier by default (glm53-flash) and auto-swaps among the elected seats by the shape of the work (deepseek-v4-pro for ordinary medium implementation, gpt-6-astra for genuinely hard work and the destructive/high-risk security-release floor tierpolicy fixes for T0). Unmatched normal fak-Ops work -> glm53-flash, the T1 middle ground.

plan.reason: destructive/irreversible tool call (delete): the security-release floor never drops to the middle tier however small the call looks -> the most careful orchestration seat gpt-6-astra (tierpolicy T0 floor beats latency/complexity)
destructive tool call (drop): same security-release floor as delete -> gpt-6-astra orchestration seat; never the fast middle-ground route for a drop-shaped call

caller tagged the aspect high-risk (push/release/migration or a security/policy surface): irreversible outward-facing work rides the gpt-6-astra orchestration seat -> exhaustive orchestration with adversarial verification, never the T1 middle ground

ultra-hard/long-horizon fak-Ops work (large refactor, migration, cross-cutting design, deep debugging) -> gpt-6-astra orchestration seat: the cost of exhaustive multi-agent orchestration is bought back by correctness on the hardest work (T0). Placed before the read/search rules so a high-flagged aspect escalates even when it is read-shaped

fak-Ops facade work: the desk attests the routed seat for the workspace surface (root turn, plan audit, view-only candidates) -> gpt-6-astra orchestration seat carries the facade; state/routed facade rows are the operator-facing triage surface

moderate fak-Ops work (ordinary feature/bugfix/focused edit) -> deepseek-v4-pro, the strong implementation seat. Named explicitly (a floor >= medium) so medium work lands on the impl seat instead of falling through to the low->glm53-flash rule below
low-complexity fak-Ops aspect (small mechanical edit, quick lookup) -> glm53-flash, the T1 middle-ground tier; reached only after the medium rule, so it bands to genuinely-low work
read-shaped tool call (read/inspect): cheap, low-stakes, not destructive and not flagged hard -> glm53-flash (fast); a wrong read costs a re-run, not a bad write
search/lookup tool call: cheap read-shaped work -> glm53-flash, the T1 middle-ground tier
short interactive fak-Ops turn (quick question/tiny edit, no complexity flag) -> glm53-flash for low latency
